Appreciate the clear ask. We can produce a one-page MAP that ties MSA redlines -> DPA review -> order form approval -> PO issuance, with owners and hard dates. Quick answers up front:

- Redwood legal can turn around annotated MSA redlines in ~3 business days once we have any customer non-standard clauses called out.
- DPA review (including data residency questions) typically takes 5–7 business days if it's only minor edits; if there are new clause asks we may need one additional review cycle.

I’ll draft MAP_v1.xlsx and share in this thread. Karthik (legal) and Priyom (CS ops) are cc’d to align on acceptance criteria and the order form variables (trial seat count, telemetry retention, SLA).

- Jul 6–9: Redwood returns annotated MSA + MAP_v1.xlsx
- Jul 10–13: DPA review cycle
- Jul 14–18: Order form finalization and DocuSign routing

Vanessa / Priyom —

Forwarding my quick internal guidance to align on precedent and items I'll push on if they surface.

Key points to prepare for MedAlign legal:
- Order form should reference the MSA signature date and specify trial pricing vs committed pricing. Avoid 'effective upon PO' language — prefer 'effective upon execution of Order Form'.
- DPA: confirm whether they require 3rd-party subprocessor list up front. If yes, we'll share our current list but ask for an evergreen acceptance process in the DPA (standard).
- Data residency: if they insist on EU-only or regionally pinned hosting, this becomes a Dedicated/private ask — call this out early.
- SLA credits: accept limited credit cap tied to monthly invoice.

Attachments for internal use: Redwood_MSA_annotated.docx — I've flagged ~6 clauses that typically see redlines.

I'll be on the call if scheduled. Priyom, please pull the pilot seat counts and a sample order form so we can estimate timing for finance.

Vanessa / Sara —

Thanks for the quick responses. A couple of clarifying notes from MedAlign legal before we jump on a call:

- We have a non-negotiable clause around data retention minimums for clinical logs — see row 3 of the attached spreadsheet (MedAlign_legal_requirements.xlsx). If Redwood can confirm parity or propose a mitigated approach (e.g., redaction + encrypted cold storage) we can proceed.
- We typically require DPA review to be signed before any production data flows. For pilot purposes we can accept an interim DPA if the order form specifies test data only and that production access is gated on a signed DPA.
- DocuSign routing: legal prefers MSA + DPA bundled in a single envelope where reasonably possible to reduce administrative friction.

Timeline constraints: our CFO wants the PO in hand by July 20; if legal review goes beyond the 2-week window we will need to escalate to procurement for an extension.

I'll join a call today at 3pm PT if that works — otherwise tomorrow morning works too.
